sources.entry: compass by dshakes - Developer-grade Claude Code + Codex configuration: cost-tiered subagents, workflow commands, guardrail hooks, MCP parity, and an installable plugin/marketplace.

summary.one_liner: A local-first configuration layer for Claude Code, Codex and Gemini that adds guardrail hooks, a hard dollar budget cap, cost-tiered subagents, and an eval-gated autonomous PR review/fix loop.
summary.what_it_does: Installs a config layer into your AI coding agent's global setup (Claude Code via symlinks into ~/.claude, with Codex and Gemini files generated from one source). Hooks block catastrophic shell commands and secret writes before they run, and auto-format edited files with an append-only audit log. A COMPASS_MAX_USD setting halts the session before the next tool call once the cap is reached, and a localhost gate proxy extends the cap to agents without hooks. A cost-tier router sends simple tasks to cheaper models, with the README claiming about 62% savings versus all-Opus on its own evalset. The README also describes a red-team scanner, a plugin-security auditor (compass audit-plugin), SLSA provenance verification, and a PR loop (review, security, tests, cross-model audit, auto-fix) that stops for a human merge.
use_cases: Cap spend on an autonomous coding agent session
Block dangerous shell commands and secret writes in Claude Code
Route simple coding tasks to cheaper models
Automate review and fix loops on pull requests
Vet third-party Claude Code plugins before installing
Share one agent config across Claude Code, Codex and Gemini
notable: Hard budget cap that halts the session before the next tool call (COMPASS_MAX_USD)
Eval-gated guardrail and red-team corpora scored in CI, reproducible with compass bench and compass redteam
Localhost gate proxy to enforce spend caps for Codex, Gemini or SDK agents
Plugin-security scanner (compass audit-plugin) for third-party plugins and marketplaces
Install replaces ~/.claude with symlinks, backs up originals first, and is reversible via make uninstall
caveats: Status is beta; the SDLC pipeline is newer and exercised via a smoke test on your own repo, and dynamic workflows are a research preview
Guardrails are described as reducing footguns, not as a security boundary; compass sandbox is the stated boundary for untrusted code
Live managed-guardrail cloud backend calls are unverified in CI and need your own credentials; the autonomous loop and fleet need model auth when opted in
